sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Smithtown, and who sets the amount?
sections.html:
The Town of Smithtown Receiver of Taxes collects every real property tax levied by the town, Suffolk County and the school districts, but does not set any rate. The Department of Assessment places a value on each parcel, and the elected boards of the school districts, county, town, villages and fire districts decide how much money they need.

The assessor's office describes the split as a pie. The levy is the whole pie, and your assessment decides only how big a slice you carry. In most cases the school district tax is the largest part of the bill, and it follows the school budget that residents vote on each May.

sections.h2: When are Smithtown property taxes due?
sections.html:
Smithtown runs a tax year from December 1 to November 30 and mails one bill around mid-December. It can be paid in full or in two halves, and the receiver says there are no grace periods on either date.

Smithtown property tax calendar, Town of Smithtown Receiver of Taxes
DateWhat happens
December 1Tax year begins
Mid-DecemberSingle annual bill mailed
January 10First half due without penalty
May 31Second half due without penalty (June 1 for 2026)
After May 31Payments go to Suffolk County
November 30Tax year ends

The extension to June 1 applied to the 2026 bill and has passed. A partial payment of at least $200 is accepted, and penalties are charged only on the remaining balance after the due date. The town cannot accept payments postmarked after May 31. After that cutoff, the Suffolk County Comptroller handles collection.

sections.h2: How do you pay a Smithtown tax bill?
sections.html:
The Receiver of Taxes is at 99 W. Main Street in Smithtown, open weekdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. with the payment window closing at 4:30 p.m., and summer hours end at 4 p.m. You can pay several ways:

  • Online by credit card or e-check, with a service fee added.
  • By phone through the automated line listed on the town page, also with a fee.
  • By mail, including the entire current bill if you want a receipt, with the district, section, block and lot numbers written on the check.
  • In person at Town Hall by check, money order, cash or credit card, with a $3.95 fee on debit cards.
  • In the drop box at the side entrance of Town Hall.

The receiver's office telephone is (631) 360-7610.

sections.h2: How does Smithtown assess property, and how do you appeal?
sections.html:
The Department of Assessment sets the fair market value of your property. If you agree you could get that amount in a sale, nothing more is needed, and if you disagree you appeal through the grievance process. Grievance Day is the third Tuesday of May.

Exemptions follow a different timetable. Applications must reach the Department of Assessment by 5:00 p.m. on March 1, except that a STAR application may be postmarked by that date. When March 1 falls on a weekend, the deadline moves to the next Monday. An approved exemption shows up on the following December bill, and denial letters go out by May 1, leaving time to grieve before Grievance Day.

A reduction won through a small claims petition is usually reflected in the tax bill. If it comes late in the year, the second half may be adjusted, and if it is too late for that, Suffolk County refunds the owner directly. The assessor's number is (631) 360-7560.

  • An increase in the rate of a taxing district.
  • A higher assessed value.
  • An exemption that expired or was not renewed.
  • A new owner who does not qualify for an exemption the seller had.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Smithtown households?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 116,847 residents for July 1, 2025, compared with 116,296 counted in April 2020. About 88.7 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, and 95 percent of residents were in the same house a year earlier.

  • Households, 2020 to 2024: 39,611, at 2.87 people each.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $669,900.
  • Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage: $3,809.
  • Median gross rent: $2,233.
  • Median household income (2024 dollars): $152,636.
  • Mean commute: 32.2 minutes.

The assessor's office lists an expired or unrenewed exemption among the reasons a bill rises, so check yours before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: Where is Smithtown, and what communities does it include?
sections.html:
Smithtown sits on the North Shore of Long Island, with Long Island Sound on its north side, Islip to the south, Brookhaven to the east and Huntington to the west. It is a large town by area, 111.5 square miles in total, but only 53.8 of those are land. Richard Smith received the Nicolls Patent in 1665, which is taken as the founding date.

Three incorporated villages sit inside the town: Head of the Harbor, Nissequogue and the Village of the Branch. The hamlets are Smithtown, Kings Park, St. James, Nesconset, and parts of Commack, Fort Salonga, Hauppauge and Lake Ronkonkoma. Several are shared with neighboring towns.

Six school districts reach into town: Smithtown Central, Kings Park Central, Commack, Hauppauge, Sachem and Three Village. The Long Island Rail Road's Port Jefferson Branch has stations at Kings Park, Smithtown and St. James. Several of these districts are shared with neighboring towns, so check the district named on your bill.

sections.h2: What should you settle with the town before selling a Smithtown house?
sections.html:
Start with the tax receiver. Ask for the amount due on your parcel, because there is no grace period on either half and unpaid balances after May 31 shift to Suffolk County. Your tax map number is printed on the bill, and the receiver asks for the district, section, block and lot on any mailed check.

Then check the Building Department at 23 Redwood Lane. It enforces the State building code and the town's zoning, issues permits and certificates of occupancy, and will search its records at no charge to see whether every permit has a matching certificate. Work done without a permit will not have one. Houses built before permits were required in 1947 can request a History Letter. A deck more than 8 inches high needs a permit, and a permit is good for one year, renewable once. The Building Department does not take applications inside the Village of the Branch, Nissequogue or Head of the Harbor. A duplicate copy of a certificate with a raised seal can be bought for a fee, and inspections are booked at (631) 360-7522.

Common permit triggers, from the department's FAQ:

  • Pools able to hold water deeper than 24 inches, with a fence of 4 to 6 feet or a self-latching gate.
  • Fences over four feet tall.
  • Detached sheds over 144 square feet and 12 feet tall; other accessory structures over 50 square feet.
  • Changes to a window header or opening width, and any skylight.
  • New gables or roof pitch, though not simple re-shingling.

Deeds are recorded at the Suffolk County Clerk's Office in Riverhead. New York's transfer tax is $2 per $500, rounded up. At the median home value of $669,900, that means $670,000 and a tax of $2,680. The seller pays unless the contract says otherwise, and Form TP-584 goes to the county clerk within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

faqs.q: When is the first half of the Smithtown tax bill due?
faqs.a: It is due by January 10 without penalty. The bill is mailed once a year in mid-December, and the receiver says there are no grace periods.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Smithtown taxes after May 31?
faqs.a: After the annual deadline, payment goes to Suffolk County. The Receiver of Taxes cannot accept payments postmarked after May 31.

faqs.q: What is the smallest partial payment Smithtown accepts?
faqs.a: The minimum is $200. Penalties apply only to the remaining balance after the due date.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Smithtown?
faqs.a: Grievance Day is the third Tuesday of May. Exemption denials are mailed by May 1, which leaves time to file.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for Smithtown exemption applications?
faqs.a: The Department of Assessment must receive applications by 5:00 p.m. on March 1. A STAR application can be postmarked on March 1, and a weekend date moves the deadline to the next Monday.
